senses.definition: (uncountable, countable) The quality or state of being sick or diseased; illness; an illness.

quotes.text: I do lament the sickness of the king.
quotes.reference: c. 1593 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedy of Richard the Third: […]”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London: […] Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act II, scene ii]:

quotes.text: Sickness is a dangerous indulgence at my time of life.

senses.definition: Nausea; qualmishness; as, sickness of stomach.
(linguistics) The analogical misuse of a rarer or marked grammatical case in the place of a more common or unmarked case.

quotes.text: We can now return to the question of how we treat the phenomenon of dative sickness (the possibility of substituting dative in place of accusative on the experiencer nominal) in Icelandic.
